experiences.name: Someone I want to become
experiences.hook: Arrive as the normal ECC avatar beside Echo, a small in-world nature/tech guide; choose whether to talk or explore.
experiences.stakes: Curiosity, identity and belonging; no penalty for skipping cosmetics.
experiences.theory: No curriculum claim for appearance choices.
experiences.action: Echo introduces experiential Year 12 learning, persona development and bringing personal experience into Career Portfolio entries. First inspect Careers and Employability Course Documents beside Echo, then hear the learning/application and persona guidance and develop the avatar. Tasks can be skipped without completion; revisit later. Explore freely, then sample the Market Experience and begin the journey. First-day card shares this sequence; local Resources documents are still pending. Personalise an avatar, explore Home Base and choose a provisional aspiration.
experiences.evidence: Usability and engagement observations only, not a curriculum mark.
experiences.recovery: Skip or replay Echo; resume dialogue locally, change appearance or aspiration later. Document availability and mission completion remain separate.
experiences.payoff: Identity, ownership and a reason to return.

experiences.participation: Planned core experience; accessible equivalent required
experiences.name: The opportunity I might miss
experiences.hook: A job you want is advertised, but your first application does not show why you fit.
experiences.stakes: The character may miss this opportunity without recognising and addressing the requirements.
experiences.theory: Job-ad requirements, response methods, cover-letter purpose and format, SAO / STAR / CAR.
experiences.action: Inspect the ad, compare a weak and strong response, learn the structure, rehearse and submit a revised application.
experiences.evidence: Annotated ad, matched criteria, cover letter and a reasoned structured response. Teacher checks relevance, not just submission.
experiences.recovery: Specific feedback, another attempt and another suitable opening. No permanent career lockout.
experiences.payoff: Greater readiness and possible story opportunity; earnings and item amounts undecided.
experiences.setting: Employer notice / application service; physical building not fixed

experiences.participation: Planned core experience; accessible equivalent required
experiences.name: Which future should I trust?
experiences.hook: Two town feeds give incompatible advice about the jobs likely to grow.
experiences.stakes: A decision based on a misleading claim may cost time or narrow the character's options.
experiences.theory: Reliable labour-market information, growth industries, comparison and bias.
experiences.action: Check source, date, place and evidence; compare industries before recommending a pathway.
experiences.evidence: Source comparison and justified recommendation, including limitations. All labour-market subtopics still need detailed task checks.
experiences.recovery: New evidence allows a revised plan; the first guess is not a permanent score.
experiences.payoff: Confidence in judgement and access to more informed options.

experiences.participation: Planned core experience; accessible equivalent required
experiences.name: The town changes overnight
experiences.hook: Automation, climate pressure, demographic change or economic shifts alter available work.
experiences.stakes: The character's original plan may no longer be sufficient.
experiences.theory: Megatrends, effects on work, adaptability, risk and decision-making.
experiences.action: Investigate the change, generate alternatives and compare retraining, relocation or a different role. A candidate class-world infrastructure project can reveal how energy or technology changes work; particular jobs and benefits require evidence.
experiences.evidence: Trend-to-impact explanation and a decision model with reasons and a review point.
experiences.recovery: Supported re-planning, not blame for an external shock.
experiences.payoff: New pathways and visible changes to work in the town.
experiences.setting: Events across existing workplaces; no mandatory Megatrends building
experiences.prerequisites: A starter plan and source-checking experience

experiences.participation: Planned core experience; accessible equivalent required
experiences.name: Our team is about to let someone down
experiences.hook: A shared task is slipping and one colleague's perspective has been overlooked.
experiences.stakes: A missed promise or poorer outcome affects the fictional team.
experiences.theory: Initiative, teamwork, diversity, active listening, non-verbal communication and time management.
experiences.action: Listen to viewpoints, clarify roles, propose an improvement, agree a plan and complete a contribution.
experiences.evidence: Teacher-observed communication and role performance, plan revisions and a reasoned reflection.
experiences.recovery: Repair the plan and rebuild trust through actions; no public popularity score.
experiences.payoff: Competence, team trust and a possible community contribution.
experiences.setting: Workplace / shared project; scale and location follow the scenario

experiences.participation: Planned core experience; accessible equivalent required
experiences.name: My plan no longer adds up
experiences.hook: Reduced shifts or an unexpected cost puts something the character cares about at risk.
experiences.stakes: A planned purchase or opportunity may be delayed unless the character adapts.
experiences.theory: Financial goals, tracking, budgeting, saving and investing, contingency and seeking assistance; life events and risk.
experiences.action: Inspect a fictional budget, seek instruction, compare options and revise the plan with a contingency.
experiences.evidence: Before/after budget, justified trade-off and support pathway. Fictional figures only; no personal family disclosure.
experiences.recovery: Support, alternative routes and another attempt remain available even at zero funds.
experiences.payoff: Preparedness and control over a revised plan; wealth is not the learning grade.

experiences.participation: Planned core experience; accessible equivalent required
experiences.name: A public profile causes a problem
experiences.hook: A fictional profile or suspicious message creates an avoidable obstacle to an opportunity.
experiences.stakes: The character risks sharing information or being misunderstood.
experiences.theory: Online safety, digital footprint, audience and bias.
experiences.action: Audit the fictional profile, identify the risk and revise privacy and communication choices.
experiences.evidence: Risk explanation and safer response. No access to students' real profiles is needed.
experiences.recovery: Correct the record and practise a safer response without humiliation.

experiences.participation: Planned core experience; accessible equivalent required
experiences.name: What should our town fund?
experiences.hook: The class treasury cannot afford every proposed improvement.
experiences.stakes: Choosing one upgrade delays another; the town needs reasons, not just votes.
experiences.theory: Consensus, evidence, communication, budgets and decision-making. The tax model is a simplified simulation, not Australian tax advice.
experiences.action: Investigate a shared class-world need; compare fictional project costs, access, benefits, job/skill implications and trade-offs; propose an allocation, explain a class decision and review the outcome. Candidate projects: repair towards flourishing, a cinema or green-energy infrastructure; none is fixed.
experiences.evidence: Proposal, budget and justification. Assess reasoning, not which project wins or who paid most tax.
experiences.recovery: Deferred proposals remain visible; absent students can contribute through an equivalent task.
experiences.payoff: A progressive upgrade in the 3D world shared by one class, potentially creating new or changing work opportunities. Exact projects, funding thresholds and relationship to Disrepair / Growth / Flourishing remain open; personal Home Base purchases are separate.
experiences.prerequisites: First prototype with a labelled simulated class fund; real sharing needs approved identity/class isolation and a teacher-controlled treasury. Cross-school/global use remains deferred under the Department safety-assessment route.

experiences.participation: Planned core experience; accessible equivalent required
experiences.name: The interview becomes real
experiences.hook: An attractive next role requires an interview format the character has not used before.
experiences.stakes: Poor preparation may cost an offer, but not the ability to keep learning.
experiences.theory: Interview types and process, preparation, greeting, responses, questions and conclusion.
experiences.action: Compare formats, rehearse with feedback and complete a teacher-observed interview.
experiences.evidence: Preparation, interview performance and reflection. Simulated dialogue alone does not evidence all verbal/non-verbal skills.
experiences.recovery: Targeted feedback and another interview opportunity.
experiences.payoff: Greater capability and a possible role offer.
experiences.setting: Workplace / interview setting; no fixed new building
experiences.prerequisites: Semester 1 application techniques; Unit 4 teaching begins

experiences.participation: Planned core experience; accessible equivalent required
experiences.name: Feedback I did not want to hear
experiences.hook: A performance review shows that effort alone has not met the role's expectations.
experiences.stakes: A responsibility or promotion may be delayed until the character responds.
experiences.theory: Handling feedback, resilience models, performance management and career change.
experiences.action: Listen, clarify, process, analyse and form an improvement plan; practise applying a resilience model.
experiences.evidence: Response to feedback, an action plan and review of progress. Not a judgement of personality or mental health.
experiences.recovery: Coaching, adjusted goals and supported re-entry after setbacks.
experiences.payoff: Growth in capability and an informed next step.
experiences.prerequisites: A shared record of fictional role expectations

experiences.participation: Planned core experience; accessible equivalent required
experiences.name: The next opportunity needs something new
experiences.hook: A new role or changed workplace needs a capability the character does not yet have.
experiences.stakes: The opportunity may be out of reach for now; training has time, cost and effort trade-offs.
experiences.theory: Lifelong learning, its career benefits and the continuing professional development cycle.
experiences.action: Identify needs, compare options, plan and undertake learning, reflect, apply and share it.
experiences.evidence: A CPD plan and evidence of learning transfer and sharing. A training purchase alone is not mastery.
experiences.recovery: Affordable alternatives, help and revised timing after setbacks.
experiences.payoff: A wider range of possible futures and useful capability.
experiences.setting: Workplace, mentor, online provider or community; dedicated hub not required
experiences.prerequisites: A meaningful capability gap and accessible learning options

experiences.participation: Planned core experience; accessible equivalent required
experiences.name: Two workplaces, two ways of living
experiences.hook: Two plausible workplaces offer different cultures, responsibilities and ways of working.
experiences.stakes: A good salary does not settle whether either role suits the character's priorities.
experiences.theory: Enterprise culture, culture types, successful characteristics and alignment with individual values.
experiences.action: Investigate workplace practices, compare evidence and explain a personally justified choice.
experiences.evidence: Culture comparison and a reasoned recommendation that considers alternatives and bias.
experiences.recovery: Plans can change; no single career, income or lifestyle earns a moral score.
experiences.payoff: Agency, self-knowledge and a chosen direction.

experiences.participation: Planned core experience; accessible equivalent required
experiences.name: Something at work is not right
experiences.hook: A fictional payslip, unsafe request or unfair treatment raises a concern.
experiences.stakes: Ignoring the issue can leave the character exposed to detriment; seeking advice is a valid action.
experiences.theory: Employment legislation, award conditions, workplace protocols and grievance processes.
experiences.action: Check appropriate current sources, document the issue, compare advice pathways and choose a justified response.
experiences.evidence: Source-grounded case response. Specific law, award rates and advice services require a fresh authoritative check when the task is written.
experiences.recovery: Teacher support, a non-personal alternative case and accessible advice; no forced trauma disclosure.
experiences.payoff: Preparedness to recognise concerns and seek appropriate help.
experiences.setting: Workplace / advice service; formal Unit 4 learning, not a Unit 3 arbitration module
experiences.prerequisites: School-safe scenario review and current official sources

experiences.time: Brief discovery; duration and frequency to test
experiences.participation: Optional; can occur throughout the year
experiences.name: A small surprise worth finding
experiences.hook: A familiar sign, an unexpected detail or a playful action reveals an original inside joke.
experiences.stakes: None; missing it never blocks learning.
experiences.action: Explore, notice a clue or perform an optional action.
experiences.evidence: Observe delight and distraction separately; no assessment claim.
experiences.recovery: No missable essential reward and no compulsory repeated search.
experiences.payoff: Small treasure, cosmetic token or funny world response; exact rewards to approve.
experiences.setting: World details chosen after the story and map are established
experiences.prerequisites: Teacher approval of joke, trigger and original assets

decisions.title: Echo guides first entry from inside the playable world
decisions.detail: Small floating blue nature/tech Echo beside the normal ECC avatar; optional short messages, no full-screen welcome. Brief intro → Course Documents → learning/persona → Avatar Studio → portfolio/exploration → Market Experience → Year 12 journey; action-paced tasks with skip and revisit. First-day card and Echo must agree. Preserve sharp rendering: prioritise entry, then prepare Studio and Market from the same local-character guidance; distant campus loads later or on explicit exploration. Automatic resolution reduction rejected 25 September. Small Careers and Employability Course Documents point beside Echo at arrival authorised; current course documents pending. Sprout, Moss and Bloom remain future intentional discovery guides. Native mesh is a local review interpretation; staged implementation and live release explicitly approved 25 September; course documents remain pending.
decisions.source: Tania explicit implementation request and follow-ups, 25 September 2026: add a small ECC Resources point; this flow needs to be in sync with Echo instructions too.
decisions.replaces: Replaces the old first-day card routing directly from saved avatar to EST Prep; does not remove EST access or approve the proposed year timetable.

decisions.title: One curriculum, one connected learning management system
decisions.detail: Career Empire is intended to deliver and manage the whole Careers and Employability curriculum through connected modes: the playable world, dedicated learning spaces, existing EST preparation, assessment and teacher support. The Blueprint is intended to become the teacher resource for delivering the year-long program, connecting curriculum, sequence, preparation, facilitation, assessment and support. Curriculum requirements drive the choice of delivery mode. A world event or productive-failure sequence is not mandatory for every activity. Preserve suitable existing EST memory cards and arcade revision before considering replacement. Results and appropriate earnings may connect back to the world, but learning evidence and game rewards remain distinct; integration rules and full LMS capabilities are not claimed implemented.

styleGuide.status: Hero environment fidelity standard approved; individual candidate appearance remains separate
styleGuide.title: A believable world, with a sense of possibility
styleGuide.ethos: Career Empire should feel like a place a young person wants to step into: recognisable, welcoming and full of possibility. Its people have warmth and personality; its buildings have substance, purpose and life inside them. Contemporary architecture, rich planting, natural materials and carefully placed technology create an optimistic near-future town. The camera brings us close enough to care. Light invites us towards an opportunity; movement makes a discovery feel earned. The world can struggle, recover and flourish without losing its identity. The ambition is the depth, craft and emotional presence of the supplied ElevenLabs Town Hall films, translated into a coherent, playable 3D world.
styleGuide.translation:
Approved hero/concept artwork is the visual north star for playable Career Empire. Target polished architectural visualisation / stylised realism: warm sandstone, glass, charcoal/blue framing, layered architecture and rooflines, pergolas/shade, rich paving, dense native Australian landscape, rocks, retaining walls and planters, strong warm directional sunlight, believable shadows/AO, environmental depth and purposeful detail.

Aim for roughly 80–90% of perceived hero richness at normal gameplay viewpoints. This is a visual acceptance ambition, not a measured percentage or current achievement. Browser optimisation must not mean simple, flat, minimal or indiscriminately low-poly.

Optimise through LOD, GPU instancing, atlases, compressed meshes/textures, PBR, normal maps, baked AO/lighting where appropriate, occlusion/frustum culling, selective geometry, distant cards/impostors, repeated modules and cheap interior impressions. Select techniques based on measurement; do not add every technique regardless of benefit.

HERO: ECC Campus, Avatar Studio and major destinations receive highest perceived fidelity. SUPPORTING: medium geometry with excellent materials and planting. BACKGROUND: aggressive LOD/impostors/cheap geometry preserving the town aesthetic.

Existing ECC is functional/blockout-quality relative to this new standard, not the final visual benchmark. Preserve recognition, working geometry and routes. Admin, Student Services and Chapel remain one connected destination. Preserve Chapel reflection and its planned wellbeing role without inventing rewards, clinical claims or curriculum triggers.
styleGuide.authority: Tania explicitly approved the governing environment standard on 13 September 2026. This supersedes earlier proposed-only environment wording. Existing character decisions and exact-asset acceptance boundaries remain.

principles.title: Modern by default; distinctive by purpose
principles.body: Use the approved ECC campus and pavilion family: warm limestone/pale brick, navy framing, timber fins, generous glass, verandas and layered native planting. Historic Town Hall art is retained comparison, not the everyday architecture target. Match material quality and human scale without duplicating every roof.

principles.title: Detailed and tactile, not photographically literal
principles.body: Use convincing stone, glass, cloth, timber, water and foliage with softened, deliberately designed forms. Keep contact shadows, consistent scale and readable silhouettes. Avoid low-detail clay placeholders as final art, shiny plastic surfaces, photographic people in a stylised town, and excessive micro-detail that disappears at play distance.

principles.title: Warm people, teen-appropriate presence
principles.body: Characters should convey curiosity, concern, confidence and recovery through expression and body language. Preserve identity from shot to shot and between studio and world. Translate the supplied pose-sheet warmth into natural 3D movement without making every character constantly smile or cheer. Do not silently replace the existing explorer's jacket with a blazer; approve wardrobe by character and context. Broaden representation through approved character designs, not random regeneration.

principles.title: Nature belongs to the town
principles.body: Use layered planting, varied grass, garden edges, water and places to pause. Integrate paths, ramps, crossings and bridges into continuous terrain. Retain the crafted richness of the selected 2D environment references, but remove their isolated tile presentation. A place should look explorable from ground level as well as understandable from above.

principles.title: Light reveals opportunity
principles.body: Use clear daylight for ordinary exploration and warm interiors against cooler exteriors for selected evening scenes. Maintain visible doors, faces and route surfaces. Cyan or teal marks useful technology and interaction; warm light suggests occupancy. Do not make every view dark blue, coat every edge in neon, or let bloom hide architecture. Night scenes are a lighting variant, not the universal palette.

principles.title: Three related visual layers
principles.body: The town is grounded and spacious. Learning tools and displays may use more focused technology effects. Rewards may briefly use stronger green, gold, cyan or violet celebration cues. Keep them recognisably related without putting a glowing reward-frame around the entire world. Colour is accompanied by symbols and readable text; the reward artwork does not determine game economics.

principles.title: The camera brings the player into the experience
principles.body: Use an aerial view to understand the town, then character-relative perspective to approach a place. Keep the destination readable, show a purposeful reaction where useful, and cross a believable threshold into a consistent interior. The supplied clips begin at ground level; the aerial-to-shoulder connection comes from earlier project guidance. Prefer steady movement over whip pans, excessive blur or unexplained cuts. Cinematics need a skip/reduced-motion alternative in the eventual game.

principles.title: Development changes care and activity, not identity
principles.body: Disrepair, Growth and Flourishing should retain the same underlying architecture, route graph and character proportions. Show weathering and reduced activity, then repair, then maintenance and life. A disruption is a separate temporary layer and personal progression is separate again. Do not turn disadvantage into ugliness or make a crisis erase all visual evidence of earned progress.

palette.name: Warm limestone
palette.role: Working campus stone interpretation; exact value not a newly approved colour specification

palette.name: Navy
palette.role: Campus frames, canopies and roofs; working interpretation

styleGuide.paletteNote: Proposed working swatches, not sampled values or official ECC brand colours. Material, lighting and skin tones must keep their natural variation. Use the authorised ECC brand source for logos and exact institutional colours; do not infer them from this small contact sheet. Violet belongs mainly to selected interface/reward accents, not a global colour wash.
avoid: Flat isometric cut-outs presented as finished 3D conversion; single textured facades used for unrestricted orbit.
A uniform town of old-fashioned civic buildings, or an equally uniform town of glass boxes.
A constantly dark neon city, permanent portal spectacle, floating holograms without purpose or strong bloom over every edge.
Miniature white display islands, oversized toy proportions, blank interiors, floating feet and doors that cannot be approached.
Uncontrolled changes to faces, hair, uniforms, badges, building footprints, doorway locations or time of day between shots.
Baked-in generated text, invented school crests, copied cultural motifs, arbitrary reward values or new gameplay mechanics hidden inside an art brief.
workflow: Choose a named reference for each job: architecture, character identity, material/lighting and camera. Attach the actual files; filenames in a prompt alone do not give a generator access to them.
Write the asset's purpose and intended experience. Lock identity, silhouette, dimensions/scale, entrance position, materials, lighting and exclusions before requesting variations.

Reuse the approved source set first. Develop the dimensioned approach and modular kit in the separate candidate; additional reference generation or vendor spending requires explicit scope and approval.

Approve one reference set, then build or commission the actual mesh, materials, rig and animation. Reuse the same geometry for states and camera shots; do not generate a different building for every frame.

Compare a rendered film reference with a real-time engine test on target school hardware. Agree measurable asset, lighting and performance budgets before production; no frame-rate or film-quality promise is made by this guide.

Record source, prompt, tool/model/version where available, date, rights, parent references, output, approval status and runtime test evidence. Keep original references and editable source aligned with the live Blueprint record.

prompts.title: Core style block
prompts.text: Career Empire: semi-realistic ECC Career Campus + Campus-to-Career Corridor for a career-and-life simulation. Attach the current CE-CAMPUS-01, CE-CAMPUS-02 and relevant CE-STUDIO-CONCEPT-01 originals; these control architecture and material treatment. Warm limestone/pale brick, navy frames, timber fins, large glass, native planting and shaded walking paths. Restrained teal interaction; warm Western Australian daylight; believable human scale, entrance and ground contact. No toy-like blockouts, constant neon, copied civic monuments, invented logos or literal claims about ECC geography. Preserve selected character identity separately. A concept is not a mesh or finished playable scene. These templates do not authorise new generation or spending.

prompts.title: Selected building to 3D concept
prompts.text: Use the Core style block. SUBJECT: [named building and reference ID]. PURPOSE: [approved experience or reference study]. Reference A controls the selected building's recognisable silhouette, materials and activity; reference B, the approved campus/pavilion concept, controls the shared material and architectural quality. Older Town Hall frames are optional historical camera studies, not current building authority. Reinterpret this design as a complete walkable building at human scale. Keep [roof profile, material accents and distinctive features]. Show [ground-level three-quarter approach / side-rear view / one step inside the entrance] in [clear daylight / agreed evening light]. Keep the entrance usable and visible, integrate continuous ground and planting, and provide credible interior depth. Preserve the same building geometry across the set. [State] changes maintenance and activity, not footprint or doorway location. No detached display base, fake paper cut-out, copied Town Hall columns on every building, or conversion into a different architectural design. This output is concept reference only, not a production model.

prompts.title: Character to cinematic 3D reference
prompts.text: Use the Core style block. CHARACTER: [approved character ID]. Attach the identity reference and outfit reference separately. Preserve the approved face, hair, skin tone, approximate age, body proportions and identity-specific details. Match the warmth and expressive clarity of the supplied character poses while using dimensional facial forms, believable cloth, groomed stylised hair and grounded contact shadows. Keep the result appropriate for a Year 12 audience; do not silently de-age the character. Outfit: [approved outfit], with the exact badge placement and left/right accessories retained. Pose/action: [one natural action]. Camera: [full-body three-quarter reference / shoulder approach / expression close-up]. No face drift, random uniform redesign, mirrored badge/watch or permanently exaggerated grin. A reference image is not a rigged 3D character.

prompts.title: Building-entry video brief
prompts.text: Use the Core style block. Attach the approved character reference, building exterior, matching interior and, only for historical camera comparison, the selected Town Hall clip. No current campus film is supplied or approved by this template. Produce a proposed 8-10 second 16:9 reference film at the tool's supported output settings. Begin behind and slightly to one side of the character, looking towards the readable entrance. Move forward smoothly with grounded footsteps; let the destination fill more of the frame. Include a short, natural reaction only if it serves the moment. Cross the actual doorway into the matching interior without passing through a wall or changing the floor plan. Keep face, hair, outfit, badge, backpack, light direction and architecture consistent. ENTRY EFFECT: [restrained doorway light by default under existing guidance; use a stronger portal only after explicit approval]. If an effect is chosen, keep it local to the doorway and keep interior depth legible. No automatic aerial opening: request that as a separate connecting shot if needed. No teleport cut, sudden day/night swap, fisheye, camera shake, foot sliding, hard strobe, geometry morph, generated captions or invented interface. This is a visual reference; game timing and interaction remain separately designed.

prompts.title: Reward or tool graphic
prompts.text: Use the same Career Empire visual family but the focused interface/celebration layer. PURPOSE: [confirmed feedback state]. Create one clear [symbol or motif] with dimensional material, a restrained luminous edge and a clean silhouette. Use [approved role colour] against [transparent or specified background]. Preserve generous clear space for separately rendered text and values. No words, numbers, school logo or invented reward amount inside the generated image. Stronger glow is allowed locally for this brief celebration, not as the environment's permanent look. Keep the symbol readable without colour alone. Confirm the requested file format and transparency from the output, not from the prompt's promise.

checks: Could this asset and the supplied Town Hall film plausibly belong in the same world?
Does it preserve the selected design while adding credible depth, scale, material and movement?
Is the important action or entrance immediately readable, with the world still visible around it?
Do the character, lighting, doorway and interior stay consistent across views and frames?
Does technology support meaning, with stronger effects reserved for a purpose?
Can the eventual playable version meet access, camera, collision, rig and school-device requirements?
Are reference preference, proposed interpretation, accepted design and tested implementation labelled separately?
openChoices: Current entry direction: restrained teal identity/wayfinding from the approved pavilion. The older film vortex does not set the everyday portal effect.
Built avatars now exist. Preserve identity references and separate Tripo/fixed-shirt, modular Body A/B and segmented schoolboy/blazer lines; no complete modular wardrobe accepted.
Current production: autonomous reversible ECC fidelity pilot, fixed-view comparison and measured optimisation, then progressive rollout by tier. Avatar/wardrobe work remains paused.
Exact measured performance budgets, faithful ECC landmarks and verified branding remain review dependencies, not settled by concept approval.

kinds.title: Decision, approval or veto
kinds.purpose: An approval can affect any domain; explicitly assess all affected domains rather than changing only the decision register.

kinds.title: Curriculum, cohort or assessment
kinds.purpose: Change the learning source and all places that represent its content or timing.

kinds.title: Activity or learning-flow change
kinds.purpose: Change the student's whole experience and its evidence/teacher path, not just an activity description.

kinds.title: Visual direction, image or film
kinds.purpose: An accepted visual change must propagate to the gallery, building/avatar records, hero/poster and production priorities.

kinds.title: Building, layout or environment
kinds.purpose: Reconcile the place's design, visual identity, purpose, routes and production state.

kinds.title: Avatar, clothing or rig
kinds.purpose: Reconcile identity/wardrobe direction, appearance, components, model/testing and every current visual placement.

kinds.title: Gameplay, economy or progression
kinds.purpose: Reconcile mechanics with the experience, rewards, evidence and protected design boundaries.

kinds.title: Implementation or bug fix
kinds.purpose: Record behavior before/after and regression proof; implementation is not approval or deployment.

kinds.title: Release, hosting or recovery
kinds.purpose: Reconcile source, deployed bytes, links/access, representative images and recovery; do not use publication as a proxy for semantic currency.

kinds.title: Research, evidence or terminology
kinds.purpose: Attach evidence to the affected claim and propagate conclusions without converting findings into unapproved decisions.

kinds.title: Workflow, audit or tracking
kinds.purpose: Repair the update mechanism and explicitly report inherited integration gaps instead of claiming the whole Blueprint is current.

kinds.title: School deployment, security, privacy or student safety
kinds.purpose: Apply the ST4S gate to all affected product, provider, data and operational changes.

changeWorkflows.completionRule: Each required surface needs a specific action or reasoned no-change result, source record IDs, owner, acceptance check and evidence. Completed changes need passed source/reader checks for every surface. Blocked or pending surfaces keep the change incomplete. Ready-for-publication is not complete: only publication may remain pending after every other required source/reader target passes. Completion requires the independent live check.
changeWorkflows.limits: These checks enforce impact coverage and evidence/freshness, not the truth of an approval or the quality of a human visual judgement. Missing originals cannot be replaced with guessed images. Unseen chats still require intake.

securityPrivacyGate.rule: Every new change requires screening of all triggers. Triggered or unknown items require full impact answers, mapped controls/tests/evidence, owner and review. Production-complete requires verified controls and tests; UNVERIFIED/LIKELY PASS never qualify.
securityPrivacyGate.historicalBoundary: Existing records remain historical; no retroactive passing stamp. Retrospective backlog covers existing features.
securityPrivacyGate.baseline: WA Department questionnaire v4c under CE-CHANGE-20260917-73; ST4S source register retained as reference/history, not the governing assessment test.

changes.title: My Life local player tracker foundation
changes.objective: Build a local work library and clear money/belongings/progress/class-world views without student identity integration.
changes.before: Economy-only lab with no work library and obsolete global-giving surface.
changes.after: My Life local tracker now has Overview, Money, Belongings, Progress, My work and Our world. Work supports titled plain-text notes/drafts/reflections, explicit save status, resume of latest active work, up to 100 preserved versions/item, preview/copy of earlier versions, reversible archive, title search, backups, current-text downloads and validated merge-as-copies imports. Money keeps prior values/schema, now requires successful persistence before showing a transaction; same-origin Web Locks used where available. Review mode never reads/writes the normal work slot. Belongings has three illustrative SVG image cards alongside the existing 3D objects. Class-world funds remain a labelled simulation; active global UI/display removed and historical ledger entries preserved.
changes.source: Tania accepts My Life local foundation, 24 September 2026.
changes.nextAction: Complete blocked browser verification and subsequent production security/data-lifecycle review.

securityPrivacyImpact.scope: New browser-local plain-text work library, revision timestamps, local backup import/export; unchanged economy key; no network or student identities.
securityPrivacyImpact.rationale: User-authored work can contain personal information. Local demo safeguards do not establish secure student storage or school approval.

answers.data: User-entered titles and plain text, self-selected type/status, local revision timestamps and archive flags. No actual student records used in verification.
answers.locations: Existing browser localStorage; explicit backup/text downloads on user device.
answers.accessCountries: No new remote processing or transmission.
answers.providers: No new provider or CDN; existing local scripts and Three.js.
answers.lifecycle: Explicit save, earlier versions preserved, reversible archive and local backups. No automatic retention expiry or permanent-delete workflow; production retention/deletion remains open.
answers.encryption: No application encryption or authenticated identity; same-browser users can inspect or edit the local work.
answers.logging: Local work revision metadata only; no telemetry or remote logging.
answers.identity: Single demo slot, no student login, author verification or account import.
answers.isolation: Separate work and economy keys; no teacher or cross-class records. This is not tenant isolation.
answers.privacySafety: Plain text rendered safely; backups schema/size checked; finished labels do not certify assessment. Do not use this preview for confidential or real student records.
answers.applicability: Existing WA Department questionnaire governs future student deployment; this does not approve classroom or cross-school use.
answers.verification: 26 Node tests pass (15 existing economy/receipt checks and 11 work-store checks). Covers revision reload, archive/restore, unchanged-save deduplication, quota failure, stale-tab conflict, corrupt-save preservation, nonpersistent review, import duplicate/collision handling, validation/limits and storage-key isolation. JavaScript syntax and HTML ID/reference checks pass. Interactive browser verification attempted twice but denied because the browser security-check service was unavailable; no workaround used. New screens, file downloads/import UI, native locks and phone layout are not browser-verified this turn.

changes.title: Economy Lab: scene-first player panel and transaction feedback
changes.objective: Continue the existing lab with a compact HUD, expandable panel and visible receipts/world consequences.
changes.before: Lab uses a permanent two-column control page and brief history entries.
changes.after: Existing Economy Lab upgraded locally: scene-first full-height layout; compact available/saved/scenario-wellbeing HUD; My life modal with Overview, Earn & try, My space, Save & give and History; J shortcut and Escape; net-pay/tax/spend receipts in the panel and world; reconstructed running balances; four animated scene viewpoints with reduced-motion support; existing owned objects/fund effects retained. No pricing, reward, tax, saved schema, campus or separate Night Market changes. Review mode avoids writing the user save.
changes.source: Explicit user target correction, 24 September 2026.
changes.nextAction: Review local presentation; publication and game integration remain separate.

securityPrivacyImpact.scope: Existing anonymous local lab state; unchanged save key/schema plus a nonpersistent review mode.
securityPrivacyImpact.rationale: Presentation change only. Local data remains untrusted; no student accounts or new provider.

answers.data: Fictional anonymous transaction choices only in this lab; no names, school IDs, response text or student records read.
answers.locations: Same browser localStorage under a separate practice key; static files and test receipts stored locally.
answers.accessCountries: No application data sent externally; this task performs no cross-country processing.
answers.providers: No new service or CDN; reuse local Three.js modules from the inspected game source.
answers.lifecycle: Explicit reset clears only the practice key; malformed saves preserved until reset; browser clearing may lose progress. Review mode does not read/write the regular save; reset is explicit.
answers.encryption: No application encryption or authenticated identity for fictional local state; anyone using this browser can inspect or edit it.
answers.logging: Versioned local transaction journal with fictional choices; no telemetry or remote logging.
answers.identity: Single local practice slot; no login and no student-account association. Multi-slot identity is proposed for the next slice.
answers.isolation: Distinct key; does not read or write legacy session/auth/avatar keys. Shared-browser users share this disposable slot; no tenant claims.
answers.privacySafety: Productive failure has free recovery and no mastery/grade inference. Wellbeing is a fictional scenario resource; not a student diagnosis.
answers.applicability: Existing WA assessment baseline retained for future production/account integration; prototype does not clear any school deployment controls.
answers.verification: 15 Node tests pass (12 existing economy invariants plus three receipt tests). Desktop and 390x844 browser checks observed pay/tax, one-time reward buttons, desk purchase and focused 3D view, savings, local/global giving, running receipt history, failure/reflection/free retry, keyboard opening and review reload.
